title: Derived tensor and actual pullback tensor arrows under section equivalence
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, and take their small pro-étale sites small relative to module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], also writing $R_T$ for its reconstructed section-ring sheaf. Let $E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\operatorname{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the fixed equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use the ordinary module operations, their specified adjunctions, and geometric composition comparisons of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data]. Use the signed direct-sum totals, K-flat complexes and derived relative tensors of [pur713-def-kflat-module, def-pc-kflat-complex, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], the derived operation comparisons of [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] and the ordinary tensor normalization of [lem-pd-section-ordinary-oplax-normalization]. The induced equivalence $D(E_T)$ identifies internal derived relative tensor with the canonical ringed K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], with its localization comparison and regular-module unit. For all derived internal $R_Y$-modules $M,N$, under these comparisons the actual derived oplax arrow $\delta_f:Lf^*(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\to Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*N$ induced by internal pullback and localization equals the canonical ringed tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The actual internal lax arrow $\mu_f=\delta_f^{-1}$ equals its inverse. These are equalities of specified natural transformations, compatible with their tensor-unit and constraint comparisons.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; canonical total-complex comparison on K-flat representatives

proof.text: For each $T$, write $Q_T$ for the section-module homotopy-to-derived localization and $\mathcal P_T$ for its full subcategory of K-flat complexes with flat terms. The exact equivalence $E_T$ identifies flat objects, K-flat complexes, acyclicity and total tensors by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Thus it identifies quasi-isomorphisms (their cohomology maps are isomorphisms under an exact equivalence). Its inverse carries $\mathcal P_T$ to internal K-flat complexes with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], every section-derived object is isomorphic to $Q_TP$ for $P\in\mathcal P_T$, and restriction to pairs of these representatives is fully faithful. Consequently these are also resolving representatives internally. Use $D(E_T)$ and its pullback comparison with resolution transformations exactly as fixed by [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. The site objects and module sections both lie in the coefficient universe $u+1$, so the hypothesis on the site in the tensor-equivalence lemma is satisfied; its sheaf-tensor hypotheses hold because [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] gives, on the small pro-étale site, the closed symmetric monoidal sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ with strong monoidal sheafification, so tensoring preserves local isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU, K-flat resolving representatives; internal/section equivalence

proof.text:
On internal representatives $P,Q$ let $t_{P,Q}:E_T\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(E_TP\otimes E_TQ)$ be the total-complex comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Conjugate its localization by the two representative tensor isomorphisms to obtain
$D(E_T)(Q_{\rm int}P\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_{\rm int}Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_TE_TP\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_TE_TQ$.
Here the internal tensor is the relative two-variable K-flat derived tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and the section tensor and its representative isomorphism are those of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Naturality of $t$ gives naturality on representatives. When a quasi-isomorphism is inverted its naturality equation can be multiplied by the inverse on either side, so the same equation holds on the localized categories. Full faithfulness of restriction in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives a unique extension $\theta_T$ to all pairs, and also extends the inverse. Their composites are identities because this holds on representatives. This proves the claimed tensor identification together with its localization comparison, rather than choosing an unrelated tensor isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YU, derived tensor and its representative comparison

proof.text: The regular module in degree zero is flat and K-flat: tensoring with it is the identity on modules and, respectively, on total complexes, via the unitors. Thus it is itself an allowed flat-term representative. The map $E_T(R_T)\cong R_{T,\rm sec}$ and both unitors are identified by [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Localizing these very maps identifies the derived regular-module unit. The internal derived associators and unitors are induced from complexes by [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]; the section ones are their corresponding total-tensor maps. On K-flat representatives the two sides of the comparison diagrams are equal because $t$ respects the ordinary associators and unitors. For a diagram in three variables, first fix two resolving representatives and use localization faithfulness in the third variable, then fix one and repeat in the second, and finally repeat in the first. The resolving localizations in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and the faithfulness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] justify each repetition. This proves the constraint comparisons for $\theta_T$ on all objects.

source.place: Tag 06YU; ordinary constraints and localization of total-tensor constraints

proof.text:
Write $F=f^*_{\rm sec}$. For $P,Q\in\mathcal P_Y$ totalize the ordinary tensor arrow of [lem-pd-section-ordinary-oplax-normalization] to obtain
$b_{P,Q}:F\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FQ)$.
The direct-sum comparison used here is the canonical one: $F$ is the specified left adjoint of [def-pd-section-module-operations-data], and $\operatorname{Hom}(F(\bigoplus A_i),B)=\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus A_i,f_*B)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(FA_i,B)$ gives its coproduct universal property. On the $(p,q)$ summand, $b$ sends $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. Naturality of the ordinary arrow with $d_P$ and $d_Q$ identifies its two differential components; both second components have the same factor $(-1)^p$ from [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Thus $b$ is a chain isomorphism, natural in both complexes. This is also the image of the actual internal total oplax arrow under $E_X,E_Y$, because the ordinary normalization asserts equality with that arrow, not just invertibility of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 07A4, totalization of the tensor-pullback isomorphism; Tag 03EL

proof.text:
Let $r_Y:Q_Y\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YP\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_YQ$ and $r_X:Q_X\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XFP\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_XFQ$ be the representative comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Pullback preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], so $r_X$ applies. Write $\epsilon_A:LF(Q_YA)\to Q_XFA$ for the specified derived-pullback comparison. Both $\epsilon_P,\epsilon_Q$ and $\epsilon_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}$ are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-tensor-pullback-computation-universes]. Put
$a=\epsilon_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}\circ LF(r_Y^{-1})$ and $c=r_X^{-1}\circ(\epsilon_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_Q)$.
Thus $a$ runs from $LF(Q_YP\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_YQ)$ to $Q_XF\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ and $c$ from $LF(Q_YP)\otimes^{\mathbf L}LF(Q_YQ)$ to $Q_X\operatorname{Tot}(FP\otimes FQ)$. All the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-comparison-descent-representatives] now hold: full faithfulness is the cited tensor descent, preservation of representatives is the cited pullback theorem, the two $r$'s are specified, $b$ is Step 4, and the required $\epsilon$'s are invertible. It gives the unique natural isomorphism whose representative component is $c^{-1}\circ Q_X(b_{P,Q})\circ a$. This is the canonical ringed tensor isomorphism: it is obtained by localizing the ordinary tensor arrow with these resolution comparisons, the construction in Tag 07A4.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; Tag 0G7E; representative descent square

proof.text: Let $\widehat\delta_f$ denote the actual internal derived oplax arrow after conjugating by $D(E_T)$, $\theta_T$ and the pullback comparison. By the meaning of the arrow induced by internal pullback and localization, its representative square has bottom arrow the localization of the ordinary internal total oplax map and vertical arrows the tensor and pullback resolution comparisons. Step 4 identifies that bottom arrow with $Q_X(b_{P,Q})$. Step 2 identifies the tensor resolution comparisons, and [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] identifies the pullback resolution transformations themselves, so the vertical arrows are precisely $a$ and $c$ of Step 5. Hence $c\circ\widehat\delta_{f,Q_YP,Q_YQ}=Q_X(b_{P,Q})\circ a$. Multiplying by $c^{-1}$ gives exactly the representative component of the ringed arrow in Step 5. Restriction to pairs of resolving representatives is faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; therefore the two specified natural transformations are equal on all derived objects. The argument compares their defining squares and does not identify maps merely because both are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 07A4, equality after the defining localization/resolution comparisons

proof.text: The inverse of the ordinary arrow on a tensor summand sends $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)$ to $st\otimes(x\otimes y)$ by [lem-pd-section-ordinary-oplax-normalization]. The two composites are identities there, so localization preserves the two inverse equations by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus the actual lax arrow $\mu_f=\delta_f^{-1}$ is carried to the inverse of the ringed arrow identified in Step 6. The unit arrow in the same ordinary normalization is scalar multiplication. Evaluate it on the degree-zero regular-module representatives of Step 3: the pullback resolution comparison is invertible on these by [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-tensor-pullback-computation-universes], and the resulting arrow is the same scalar multiplication on both sides. The ordinary associator and unitor compatibility is part of the ordinary normalization. Totalization respects those equations, since on each summand the maps are those ordinary maps with the same degrees and signs as in Step 4. Apply the one-variable localization faithfulness of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] successively in each variable, as in Step 3, using the resolving representatives of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. This proves the tensor-unit and constraint compatibility of the identified natural transformations.
